# Volume 3 — Chapter XXIX Isolde’s Wedding

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

“When all is said and done, pink ones are the sole genuine roses,” Nell remarked, while binding the bouquet of Isolde with white ribbon inside the gable facing westward at Pear Hill. “Love and faith find their bloom in them.”
{: #nw-v03-c29-p0000 }

In the center of the room, Isolde stood anxiously, dressed in her wedding white, with her dark ringlets dusted by the sheer material of her bridal veil. Nell had placed that veil upon her, honoring the emotional agreement they had made years earlier.
{: #nw-v03-c29-p0001 }

“Things are mostly how I envisioned them a long time back, during the days I cried because of your unavoidable wedding and the separation that would follow for us,” she chuckled. “Isolde, you match the bride in my fantasies, complete with that ‘lovely misty veil’; meanwhile, I am serving as your bridesmaid. However, oh dear! My sleeves aren't puffed—even if the short lace pair I am wearing look better. Furthermore, my heart isn't completely shattered, and I don't precisely despise Gideon.”
{: #nw-v03-c29-p0002 }

“It isn’t truly a separation, Nell,” Isolde objected. “My new home won't be distant. Our affection for one another will remain just as strong. That friendship ‘oath’ we pledged so many years ago has never been broken by us, has it?”
{: #nw-v03-c29-p0003 }

“Yes. We have preserved it loyally. Isolde, our companionship has been lovely. Not a single disagreement, chilliness, or harsh remark has ever ruined it; and my wish is for it to remain that way forever. However, matters are unable to stay entirely unchanged following this. You will possess different pursuits. My place will merely be on the periphery. Still, as Mrs. Agatha remarks, ‘such is life.’ Mrs. Agatha has presented you with a cherished knitted quilt featuring the ‘tobacco stripe’ design, and she states that she will bestow one upon me as well whenever I get married.”
{: #nw-v03-c29-p0004 }

“The unkind aspect of your upcoming wedding is my inability to serve as your bridesmaid,” Isolde mourned.
{: #nw-v03-c29-p0005 }

“Next June, when Cressy weds Mr. Hale, I am scheduled to serve as her bridesmaid, after which I have to cease, because you are aware of the saying ‘three times a bridesmaid, never a bride,’” remarked Nell, looking out the window past the pink and white blooms of the orchard below. “Isolde, the minister is approaching.”
{: #nw-v03-c29-p0006 }

“Oh, Nell,” Isolde puffed out, all at once growing extremely white-faced and starting to shake. “Oh, Nell—I am terribly anxious—I am unable to carry on—Nell, I am certain that I shall lose consciousness.”
{: #nw-v03-c29-p0007 }

“I will haul you over to the rainwater hogshed and plunge you inside if you do,” Nell remarked without sympathy. “Be of good cheer, my sweet. Marrying cannot be exceedingly dreadful if such a great number of individuals live through the service. Observe my calm and collected demeanor, and draw bravery from it.”
{: #nw-v03-c29-p0008 }

“Hold on until it is your turn, Miss Nell. Oh, Nell, my ear catches father walking up the stairs. Hand me my bouquet. Is my veil positioned correctly? Do I look extremely pale?”
{: #nw-v03-c29-p0009 }

“You look truly beautiful. Izzy, my dear, give me a final farewell kiss. Never again will Isolde Pembroke kiss me.”
{: #nw-v03-c29-p0010 }

“However, Isolde Duckett is going to. Look, mother is shouting for us. Let's go.”
{: #nw-v03-c29-p0011 }

Adhering to the straightforward, traditional custom common at the time, Nell descended to the drawing room leaning on Hugh’s arm. Having arrived just that day, Hugh had not seen her since their departure from Portmaris until they encountered each other at the stairhead. Hugh extended a polite handshake. He appeared to be in good health, even if, as Nell observed right away, he seemed somewhat lean. Far from being pale, a color had flared upon his cheek when Nell had approached him in the corridor, dressed in her gentle white gown with lilies-of-the-valley tucked into the glowing piles of her hair. When the pair stepped into the filled parlor, a faint hum of approval swept through the gathered guests. “What a fine-looking pair they are,” murmured the easily touched Mrs. Agatha to Thirza.
{: #nw-v03-c29-p0012 }

Gideon strolled inside by himself, his countenance extremely flushed, after which Isolde entered grandly attached to the arm of her father. She avoided passing out, and no improper incident happened to disrupt the service. A period of eating, drinking, and celebrating came next; afterwards, when night was drawing to a close, Gideon and Isolde traveled by carriage under the moonlight toward their place of residence, while Hugh accompanied Nell on a walk to Grey Shutters.
{: #nw-v03-c29-p0013 }

A bit of their former fellowship had come back amid the relaxed gaiety of the night. Ah, walking along that familiar path alongside Hugh once more felt wonderful!
{: #nw-v03-c29-p0014 }

Because the night was exceptionally quiet, a person ought to have caught the rustle of blooming roses, the giggling of daisies, the chirping of grass—numerous lovely noises, entirely blended with one another. The splendor of the moonlit sky over well-known fields illuminated the earth.
{: #nw-v03-c29-p0015 }

“Could we not go for a walk along Lovers’ Lane before you head inside?” Hugh inquired while the pair traversed the bridge spanning the Lake of Glassy Waters, wherein the moon rested like a huge, sunken flower of gold.
{: #nw-v03-c29-p0016 }

Nell gave her prompt agreement. Lovers’ Lane existed as a genuine trail in a realm of magic that evening—a glistening, secretive area, brimming with sorcery within the pale-spun spell of moonbeams. There was an earlier period during which taking a stroll like that alongside Hugh along Lovers’ Lane would have proved much too perilous. However, Cyril and Rowena had rendered it exceedingly secure at present. Nell caught herself giving a great deal of thought to Rowena while she conversed pleasantly with Hugh. She had encountered her on a few occasions prior to departing Portmaris, and she had acted delightfully amiable toward her. Rowena had likewise acted delightfully amiable. In truth, they formed an exceptionally warm couple of individuals. Yet despite this, their familiarity had failed to develop into a close bond. Clearly, Rowena did not qualify as a soulmate.
{: #nw-v03-c29-p0017 }

“Will Brierley be your location for the whole summer?” Hugh inquired.
{: #nw-v03-c29-p0018 }

“No. I’m heading down east to Coombe Road next week. Esther Haythorne wants me to cover her teaching throughout July and August. They run a summer term at that school, and Esther is unwell. Therefore, I will be substituting for her. In a way, I don't mind. Do you realize that I am starting to feel somewhat like an outsider in Brierley these days? It saddens me—yet it is real. It is truly dreadful how many children have grown into big boys and girls—actual young men and women—over the last two years. Half of the students I taught are now adults. Seeing them occupying the spots that you and I and our friends once held makes me feel terribly ancient.”
{: #nw-v03-c29-p0019 }

Nell chuckled and breathed a sigh. She considered herself to be extremely aged, adult, and sagacious—a feeling that merely demonstrated her youthfulness. She asserted to herself that she yearned immensely to return to those cherished joyful times when existence was viewed via a pink haze of expectation and fantasy, and held an elusive quality that had vanished eternally. Where had it gone now—the splendor and the vision?
{: #nw-v03-c29-p0020 }

“‘Thus the world wags on,’” Hugh cited with a practical and somewhat distracted air. Nell questioned whether Rowena occupied his thoughts. Ah, Brierley would become extremely desolate from this point forward—now that Isolde had departed!
{: #nw-v03-c29-p0021 }
